clue.text: Like the immutable laws of design?

definitions.text: Like the immutable laws of design?

blocks.note: surface reading: the unchangeable laws handed down to Moses, which can be described with an adjective from his name
setter's reading: the same adjective names a decorative picture made from small pieces of tile or glass

explanation.surface: A philosopher wonders whether the rules of good design are fixed for ever.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mosaic law is the law of Moses, famously unchangeable; a mosaic is also a design of inlaid pieces, so the one adjective covers both halves.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means relating to Moses, whose commandments are the classic immutable laws, and as a noun it is a tiled pattern.

clue.text: Deliveries come up to scratch using the high road

blocks.note: in cricket an over is a set of six deliveries bowled from one end
to pass is to reach the required standard

explanation.surface: Parcel deliveries meet the standard by taking the main road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deliveries' looks like the post; in cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled, each a delivery.
explanation.definitionFit: An overpass is a road or bridge carried over another, so it is literally the higher road at a junction.

clue.text: Acquiescent woman interrupting stroll

indicators.note: something interrupting breaks into the middle of another, so it goes inside

blocks.note: to amble is to stroll
Ena is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A compliant woman breaks into someone's leisurely walk.
explanation.walkthrough: AM(ENA)BLE: the woman's name breaks into the stroll.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone acquiescent goes along with things readily, so they are willing, compliant and easily persuaded.

clue.text: Courses run by university in crucial reorganisation

indicators.note: a reorganisation puts things into a new order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
U is the abbreviation for university
taken as written

explanation.surface: Degree courses get a vital shake-up from the university that runs them.
explanation.walkthrough: R and U join the letters of crucial, and all nine are rearranged together.
explanation.definitionFit: Curricula is the Latin plural of curriculum, a programme of study, so it means courses taught at a school or college.

clue.text: Disconsolate master heading round loaded vessel

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its front, so only its opening letter is wanted

blocks.note: first letter of master
a round shape is the letter O
a vessel loaded to the brim holds an urnful

explanation.surface: A gloomy ship's master heads off round a heavily laden boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a ship to go with 'master', but here it is an urn, and the loaded urn is an urnful, a word's worth of quantity.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone disconsolate cannot be comforted, and grief of that kind is exactly what a sorrowful, grieving person feels.

clue.text: Queen, or king, that's given exceptional attention in West

indicators.note: exceptional means out of the ordinary, so the letters are put out of their usual order
in places everything so far inside the next piece

blocks.note: R for rex, Latin for king
i.e., id est, means that is
the nine letters of attention rearranged
Mae West, the American film star

explanation.surface: A queen, or a king, who receives special attention in the western world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'West' with a capital is the film star Mae West, not the compass direction; i.e. (id est) is the standard abbreviation for 'that is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Marie Antoinette was the queen of France married to Louis XVI, guillotined in the Revolution in 1793.

clue.text: Causing a disturbance, giving port to you and me

blocks.note: Rio de Janeiro, the Brazilian port
taken as written
you and me together are us

explanation.surface: Someone causes a scene by handing a glass of port to the two of us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' looks like the drink but is a harbour city.
explanation.definitionFit: Riotous behaviour is wild and disorderly, the kind of conduct that creates an uproar or public disorder.

clue.text: Set alight gold candlestick

blocks.note: flambé: food doused in spirit and set alight
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: Someone lights a golden candle holder.
explanation.walkthrough: Flambé is the cooking term for food set alight in brandy; the accent drops in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: A flambeau is a flaming torch, and by extension a large ornamental branched candlestick.

clue.text: In the French it leads to lively linguistic proficiency

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another
leads to says the next piece follows straight on

blocks.note: le is French for the
taken as written
racy means lively and spirited

explanation.surface: Speaking French leads to a lively mastery of language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the French' reads as 'in French', but 'the French' is the French word for the, with 'it' placed in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Literacy is the ability to read and write, a basic competence with language.

clue.text: Never caught by change of tack, he puts on a coat

indicators.note: something caught by another is held inside it, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: ne'er is the poetic contraction of never
to veer is to change course, as a sailing boat does when it changes tack

explanation.surface: A man who never changes his approach still manages to put his coat on.
explanation.walkthrough: Ne'er is the poetic contraction of never; sailors veer when they change tack. A veneerer's 'coat' is a thin layer of wood, not clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A veneerer applies a thin decorative layer of wood over furniture, which is putting a surface coat on it.

clue.text: Angry about restriction in an antipodean port

indicators.note: about means surrounding here, so one word wraps around the other

blocks.note: hot under the collar, hot-tempered
a bar is a restriction or ban

explanation.surface: Someone in an Australian harbour town fumes about the rules imposed on them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Antipodean' means Australian or New Zealand, from the British point of view on the opposite side of the globe.
explanation.definitionFit: Hobart is the capital and harbour city of Tasmania, in Australia, which lies at the antipodes from Britain.

clue.text: Would that we were in the mood!

definitions.text: Would that we were in the mood!

blocks.clueFragment: Would that we were in the mood!
blocks.note: surface reading: a sigh of someone wishing they felt like doing something
setter's reading: mood is the grammatical term, and 'would that' is how English voices the mood of wishing

explanation.surface: A wistful couple wish they felt up for something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mood' is grammar, not feeling: the whole clue is an example of a wish, and the verb mood that expresses wishes is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar the optative mood expresses a wish, as Greek verbs do and as English does with phrases like 'would that' or 'if only'.

clue.text: Bishop wearing flowing vestment runs after thief

indicators.note: a person wearing a garment is inside it, so one piece goes within another
after places the following piece at the end, behind what came before

blocks.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
a long loose robe, as a cleric wears
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A robed bishop chases after a burglar.
explanation.walkthrough: The bishop goes inside the robe, ROB(B)E, then R is added to make ROBBER.
explanation.definitionFit: A robber is someone who steals, so the word is a plain synonym for a thief.

clue.text: A player's forte, giving rise to brash vulgarity

blocks.note: first meaning: forte in music is the instruction to play strongly, at volume
second meaning: showiness and garishness, as of loud clothes

explanation.surface: A performer's strong point turns out to be crude showing off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forte' looks like a strength or talent, but it is the musical marking meaning loud.
explanation.definitionFit: Forte is volume in music, and the same noun also describes garish, vulgar showiness, as of loud colours or manners.

clue.text: Quiet girl represented in stories of earthly paradise

indicators.note: something represented is shown in a new form, so the letters are rearranged
in puts the rearranged piece inside the next one

blocks.note: sh is the call for quiet
the four letters of girl rearranged
ana is a collection of anecdotes or sayings

explanation.surface: A shy girl appears in tales of heaven on earth.
explanation.walkthrough: SH + AN(GRIL)A. Ana, meaning a collection of stories or table talk, is a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Shangri-La is the hidden Himalayan valley utopia of James Hilton's novel Lost Horizon, now any idyllic retreat.

clue.text: Passage avoiding a detached territory

indicators.note: avoiding something means leaving it out, so a letter is dropped

blocks.note: an aisle is a passage between seats
taken as written, the letter to remove

explanation.surface: A route skirts around a separate stretch of land.
explanation.definitionFit: An island is land cut off from the rest by water, so it is territory standing apart from the mainland.

clue.text: One man is on treatment for sleeplessness

indicators.note: treatment works something over, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
the seven letters of man is on rearranged

explanation.surface: A single man is receiving treatment because he cannot sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: Insomnia is the chronic inability to fall or stay asleep, so it is the medical name for sleeplessness.

clue.text: Transporter making deliveries, in the main

definitions.text: Transporter making deliveries, in the main

blocks.note: surface reading: a delivery van, mostly doing its rounds
setter's reading: the main is the sea, and the deliveries are rescues of people saved from it

explanation.surface: A van spends most of its time on delivery runs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the main' looks like 'mostly'; the main is an old word for the open sea, and delivery is rescue.
explanation.definitionFit: A lifeboat is a vessel launched to rescue people in distress at sea, delivering them from danger.

clue.text: Polish youth leader's girl

indicators.note: the leader of a word is the letter at its front

blocks.note: to rub is to polish
first letter of youth

explanation.surface: The girlfriend of a young man who leads a group from Poland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' with a capital looks like the nationality; it is the verb, to shine.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruby is a girl's given name, and crosswords often define names simply by girl or boy.

clue.text: Note new list of facts is obtainable from letter

blocks.note: re, the second note of the sol-fa scale
N is the abbreviation for new
a table sets out facts in rows and columns

explanation.surface: A short note brings a fresh fact sheet that came in a letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letter' is not post: a letter is one who lets out property, a landlord.
explanation.definitionFit: A rentable property is available to hire, so it can be had from a landlord who lets it out.

clue.text: Maintained a stable equilibrium, just

blocks.note: first meaning: kept steady without toppling, a past-tense verb
second meaning: fair and even-handed, an adjective

explanation.walkthrough: 'Just' at the end reads like 'only barely'; it is the adjective meaning fair.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is the past tense of the verb for holding steady, and also an adjective for a fair, impartial judgement.

clue.text: Wilful damage causing boats to founder some time afterwards

indicators.note: to founder is to sink and break up, so the letters are wrecked and rearranged
afterwards says the next piece comes later, at the end

blocks.note: the five letters of boats rearranged
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Deliberate vandalism makes the boats sink some while later.
explanation.definitionFit: Sabotage is deliberate destruction or obstruction, carried out on purpose, as of machinery or a plan.

clue.text: No news broadcast about students affected by inflation

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are scattered into a new order
about means around here, so the rearranged word goes round the rest

blocks.note: the four letters of news rearranged
O, nought, means none
L is a learner, so two learners are students

explanation.surface: A news bulletin says nothing about students struggling with rising prices.
explanation.walkthrough: L stands for learner, as on British learner-driver plates, so two Ls make students. 'Inflation' suggests prices but means being puffed up.
explanation.definitionFit: Something swollen is puffed up, as if inflated, so being blown up larger matches being affected by inflation.

clue.text: Order regiment forward for the king

blocks.note: the OBE is the Order of the British Empire
R is an abbreviation for regiment
on as in onward, moving forward

explanation.surface: An officer commands the regiment to advance on the king's behalf.
explanation.walkthrough: The OBE is a British honour, the Order of the British Empire.
explanation.definitionFit: Oberon is the king of the fairies in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream, so he is 'the king' in a literary sense.

clue.text: The bird to sound discordant after dark

indicators.note: after puts the first-named piece behind the other one

blocks.note: the dark of night
to jar is to make a harsh, grating sound

explanation.surface: A bird starts screeching once it gets dark.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is fair to the bird itself: this night-flying bird is named for its churring call at dusk.
explanation.definitionFit: The nightjar is a nocturnal bird, a goatsucker, known for its whirring, churring song heard at dusk.

clue.text: Fool served in a restaurant

definitions.note: describes something served rather than naming it

blocks.note: first meaning: a silly person, a simpleton
second meaning: a strip of pasta dished up in an eatery

explanation.surface: A dessert of whipped fruit cream is on the restaurant menu.
explanation.walkthrough: A fool is also a British pudding of fruit and cream, which the surface leans on; the answer is the silly person and the pasta.
explanation.definitionFit: Noodle is an old informal word for a simpleton, and also the pasta strip served in many restaurants.

clue.text: Heads of legation irate at traffic hold-up?

blocks.note: surface reading: senior diplomats fuming in a jam
setter's reading: the heads of legation, irate, at and traffic read as the letters L, I, A, T, and the answer itself, split in two, is the instruction that turns them round

explanation.surface: Ambassadors lose their temper stuck in a traffic jam.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: read TAIL BACK as an instruction, TAIL reversed, and it gives LIAT, the heads of 'legation irate at traffic'. The question mark flags this back-to-front wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A tailback is a long queue of vehicles stretching back from an obstruction, a British word for a traffic jam.

clue.text: A northern state with a point, they feel

blocks.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for northern
Tenn is the abbreviation for Tennessee, a US state
taken as written
E for east, a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Residents of a northern state with a purpose have feelings.
explanation.definitionFit: Antennae are an insect's feelers, the sensory organs on its head that touch and sense its surroundings.

clue.text: Notices about people requiring compensation

indicators.note: about means around here, so one word wraps the other

blocks.note: ads, advertisements, are notices
men are people

explanation.surface: Posters about people seeking damages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Requiring' only links; the definition is the single last word.
explanation.definitionFit: To make amends is to give reparation for a wrong, so the noun means redress or compensation.
